subject: Re: Pilot acceptance — cost bridge & batching spec
body:
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@clarionhealth.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@clarionhealth.com>
Date: 2025-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot cost acceptance — quick sync

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday. The Clarion evaluation team is ready to lock a pilot start date (targeting week of Oct 6) but procurement asked us to confirm the economic guardrails before we sign the MAP.

Specifically they want a short, auditable "cost bridge" showing: tokens/$ baseline we used for the pilot estimate, assumed cache hit-rate, batching parameters (max latency / target batch size), and how we will report actuals vs projected (per-week). They also want to know which savings are treated as bill credits vs x-day stabilization adjustments.

Could your team produce a one-pager + the CSV of assumptions by EOD Monday? Also: is there a recommended acceptance gate we should put in the MAP (e.g., if realized tokens/$ > 20% above estimate after 2 weeks we pause)?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m tomorrow if that helps.

Sam
Director, Product — Clarion Health

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@clarionhealth.com>
Cc: Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@clarionhealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-09-14T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot cost acceptance — quick sync

Sam — appreciate the clear ask. Attached are two artifacts: 1) a one-page "cost bridge" draft (clarion_map_draft_v2.pdf) that maps our estimate to the line items you asked for, and 2) a CSV of the batching/cache assumptions we used for the estimate (batching_cache_assumptions.csv).

High level summary (for the MAP):
- Pilot baseline: 1.2M generated tokens / month = $2,160 projected (assumes $0.0018 per generated token for the chosen quantized variant).
- Cache assumptions: 45% steady-state KV prefix hit rate assumed for routing of conversational reuse (we conservatively modeled 35–55% in the spreadsheet).
- Batching: typical request window 30ms; recommended target batch size 6 for 95th%-latency <= 220ms. We included a burst policy that allows short spikes up to batch size 20 for 5% of requests.
- Stabilization and credits: we propose a 14-day stabilization window. Any realized per-token cost improvement after day 14 (compared to the running 14-day baseline) is eligible for retroactive credits; overruns in the first 14 days are treated as "observation variance" and not automatically credited.

Proposed MAP gating language (draft):
- Acceptance gate: if realized average tokens/$ for production traffic exceeds the projected value by >20% for 2 consecutive 7-day windows after the 14-day stabilization, Clarion and Redwood will trigger a joint review and may pause promotion to production until corrective actions (caching tuning, model variant switch, or traffic shaping) are implemented.

I've looped in Karthik to validate the cache/batching numbers and Lauren for the suggested billing language. If that reads ok I'll push the draft MAP to the Drive link and we can iterate.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment(s): clarion_map_draft_v2.pdf, batching_cache_assumptions.csv

On 9/14/25 11:02, priyom_das@redwood.ai wrote:
> Proposed MAP gating language (draft):
> - Acceptance gate: if realized average tokens/$ for production traffic exceeds the projected value by >20% for 2 consecutive 7-day windows after the 14-day stabilization...

Quick technical verification and a few clarifying notes from engineering:
- Cache hit-rate: our SDK + runtime instrumentation shows that for Clarion-like conversational flows (short prompts plus history reuse), a conservative steady-state hit of 40–50% is realistic with two changes: prefix-keying enabled and a 48-hour cache TTL. The CSV models 35/45/55% which is a good bracket.
- Batching latency trade-offs: target batch=6 => median latency savings ~18% vs batch=1; 95th%-tile latency target ~220ms depends on request distribution. If Clarion expects bursts (campaigns or scheduled jobs), enable the burst policy but cap billed burst throughput separately to avoid open-ended cost risk.
- Model variant: the estimate used a 4-bit quantized LLaMA-family variant we validate in our bench. Switching to a lower-precision variant yields material tokens/$ improvements but increases risk of quality regression; recommend running the QA prompt set in qa_prompt_set.txt during the 7-day pre-promote window.
- Example quick math (steady-state model): 
  * Price per generated token (q4) = $0.0018
  * Effective tokens generated per user request (avg) = 240
  * Cache hit reduces generation by 45% => effective billed tokens/request = 132
  * Effective price/request = 132 * $0.0018 = $0.2376

I can produce a one-page micro-runbook for the engineering acceptance checks (latency checks, cache telemetry thresholds, and a list of fast rollback steps) if that helps the MAP.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — a few procurement/ops notes from my side:
- Clarion's procurement requires any retro-credit mechanics to be explicitly capped (e.g., max credit equal to 30% of the pilot invoice) so we should include a cap in the MAP.
- For billing cadence: Clarion prefers weekly usage reports and a sample invoice for the pilot week 3 to validate our reporting.
- We should also define a per-request SLA (availability + P95 latency target) that gates crediting and promotion. Karthik, can you attach the P95 numbers for the batch=6 config to the runbook?

Neha Kapoor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with what procurement asked for. Two quick additions before we finalize:
1) Add a guardrail in the MAP that clarifies "prefetch/prediction" savings (where we reduce billed generation via intelligent prefetch) are eligible for credits only after a 14-day stabilization AND after the Clarion QA team signs off on quality for the reduced-path outputs.
2) Clarion would like a short monthly cost readout (15m) during the pilot with a slice for weekend heavy-usage (we saw spikes in last year's trials).

Can we do a quick 20m tomorrow (9/17) at 10:00am PT to sign off? If so I'll circulate a calendar invite and sign the MAP afterward.

Best,
Megan Ortiz
VP, Platform — Clarion Health
